cut_items.item: Open PRs update automatically after force push, but line comments may lose anchors and reviewers may need to re-review
Protected branches like main/master usually reject force pushes anyway
Open PR updates automatically after force push; reviewers may need to re-review because line comments can lose anchors after a rebase
Protected branches usually reject force pushes anyway
Advises looking at unfamiliar commits shown by git log before overwriting

added_items.item: If --force-with-lease is rejected, someone pushed new commits: fetch, review, and rebase onto them again before retrying
Teammates sharing the branch must fetch and rebase onto or reset to the new history, otherwise their next push can bring the old commits back
Alternative for shared branches: merge the target branch into the feature branch instead of rebasing so a normal push works
Empty output from git log HEAD..origin/<branch> means no commits would be lost
Lost commits from plain --force are hard to recover
Also avoid force pushing shared branches such as develop
